findings.title: Whitespace normalization erases executable newlines and exact approval identity

evidence.detail: normalizeCommand collapses all whitespace, including quoted text and newlines.
hashCommand hashes the collapsed string while claiming exact command binding.
Classification normalizes before the newline-aware scanner.
Only a nonempty classification enters high-impact authorization.
Full-log basher execution itself constructs a multiline shell wrapper.

findings.trigger: Use a newline-separated assistant command such as printf safe followed by a Python -c one-liner; alternatively change internal whitespace in an approved quoted payload.
findings.consequence: A real full-access terminal probe executed both harmless statements with zero authorization calls. Two distinct quoted Node payloads produced identical action, target, and command hash, so the receipt comparison cannot distinguish their bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Hash the exact executable bytes; parse the original command without flattening shell separators or quoted operands. Keep any display normalization separate from authority.
findings.acceptanceProbe: A newline-separated high-impact second command reaches authorization in balanced and strict modes; approvals for quoted payloads differing by a space or newline are rejected as mismatches.

findings.title: The first classified effect masks later high-impact effects in a compound command

evidence.detail: Compound classification returns immediately on the first recognized segment.
Balanced mode only examines the single action handed to it.
Production authorization evaluates that single classification.

findings.trigger: Put a routine recognized action before a risky effect, for example npm install fixture && rm -rf fixture, or git push origin feature && terraform apply.
findings.consequence: Pure production-function probes classified only dependency-install or push and returned allowed with approvalRequired:false; later deletion/deployment is never evaluated. The defect also applies inside recursively inspected shell payloads.
findings.suggestedFix: Represent and evaluate every executable effect, including substitutions and wrappers, then authorize the entire immutable plan against all relevant action/target pairs.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Vary the ordering of routine, destructive, remote, and deployment segments: every risky effect requires the expected decision, and no earlier routine command suppresses it.

findings.title: Balanced mode allows force and delete pushes to feature branches

evidence.detail: Push parsing retains only action push, branch and target; destructive flags are not risk attributes.
The balanced high-impact set excludes push.
Push approval is conditional only on a known default-branch match.
Product policy explicitly retains force/delete/default-branch push gating.

findings.trigger: Under balanced mode issue git push --force origin feature or git push --delete origin feature.
findings.consequence: Both production policy probes return allowed without approval. The bundled full-access producer intentionally leaves these decisions to the separate harness gate, so the optional git-commit profile is not a fallback protection here. No remote command was executed.
findings.suggestedFix: Carry force, delete, refspec, and ambiguous target information into push risk evaluation; preserve routine feature pushes and the explicit allow-all choice.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Probe -f, --force-with-lease, --delete, plus-prefixed and deletion refspecs, default-branch destinations, and ambiguous upstream pushes in all three modes.

findings.title: Canonical provider credentials are stripped for terminal commands but inherited by adjacent launchers

evidence.detail: Raw system environment must not be handed to child processes.
Compiler runner inherits by omission or merges raw host environment with overrides.
LSP spawns with cwd alone, implicitly inheriting the host environment.
Chrome pipe launcher omits an explicit child environment.
Tool version probes inherit the host environment.
SCIP launcher also omits an explicit child environment.

findings.trigger: The host has a canonical BYOK key and runs a diagnostic/compiler, language server, browser, or discovery/index subprocess.
findings.consequence: A harmless Python child saw the synthetic OPENAI_API_KEY under both diagnostic inheritance and override paths; the terminal child saw neither sentinel. These launchers can disclose credentials that the terminal helper and credential denylist promise to withhold.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a shared environment constructor on implicit host-environment launch paths, scrub after merges, and make intentional credential delegation explicit. Preserve ordinary project variables and MCP server credentials deliberately configured by the host.
findings.acceptanceProbe: For every launcher test canonical host keys and attempted reinjection with harmless sentinels, while verifying PATH/project variables and explicit authorized server credentials still behave correctly.

findings.title: Shell leader exit cancels escalation while descendants remain alive

evidence.detail: Timeout/abort begins group TERM with a five-second KILL timer.
Shell close settles the operation and clears the escalation timer.
Any background settlement clears its pending escalation.
Leader exit settles the background job stopped.
A settled job refuses subsequent kill attempts.

findings.trigger: A command creates a TERM-ignoring child with redirected output, then waits; cancellation or a finite timeout kills the shell leader first.
findings.consequence: After 5.5 seconds the SYNC result was timedOut while its child remained sleeping. BACKGROUND reported stopped while its child remained sleeping, and a later SIGKILL request returned killed:false. These were ordinary process-group descendants, not escaped sessions.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep process-scope termination supervision independent of leader close and registry settlement; confirm the owned scope is empty before claiming completion, or report an explicit uncertain/live-descendant state.
findings.acceptanceProbe: For timeout, abort, and kill use redirected-output children that ignore TERM; verify group KILL still happens after leader exit and no child remains after the grace period. Add platform-specific guarantees without changing unbounded defaults.

findings.title: Output-quota failure makes a live background process unkillable through its job

evidence.detail: Quota breach settles the job as terminal error before signaling.
Quota path sends TERM without scheduling KILL escalation.
killBackgroundJob refuses every state except running.
Existing quota test checks registry error and log size, not OS process death.

findings.trigger: A background process exceeds the 10 MiB log quota and ignores TERM.
findings.consequence: The probe log was bounded at 10,485,760 bytes, but after 5.5 seconds its process was still sleeping. A SIGKILL request through the job returned killed:false because status was already error.
findings.suggestedFix: Record quota failure separately from process liveness, retain kill authority while the process is alive, and run bounded TERM/KILL cleanup before dropping the handle.
findings.acceptanceProbe: A TERM-ignoring output flood becomes an error with bounded logs and confirmed dead process scope; a user kill remains effective while quota cleanup is pending.

findings.title: MCP client eviction drops registry entries without closing their transports

evidence.detail: The stated 64-client cap is intended to bound open processes/transports.
Eviction deletes keys and caches without invoking close.
Connected clients are registered after transport initialization.

findings.trigger: More than 64 distinct MCP server configurations are connected over the host process lifetime.
findings.consequence: A fake-connect probe registered 65 real Client objects and observed zero close calls at eviction. Real transports remain open after their registry entry disappears; this is an inference from the same path and the dependency transport lifecycle, not a measurement of 65 live subprocesses.
findings.suggestedFix: Give cached clients explicit leases and disposal; close idle evicted clients and refuse or defer eviction of active clients rather than abandoning live transports.
findings.acceptanceProbe: At the client cap, observe exactly one appropriate idle transport close while leased requests continue; verify stdio children/sockets terminate and no lost handle remains.

findings.title: Configured hook effects have no production approval context

evidence.detail: Default hook executor is runTerminalCommand.
Hook calls do not supply a host profile or high-impact authorizer.
Production hook dispatch supplies environment/signal/fs but no approval seam.
Targeted validation delegates to this same hook path.

findings.trigger: A user-configured hook uses a classified harmless one-liner or another action needing authorization.
findings.consequence: The injected Python print hook returned approvalRequired and permissionDenied with workspace-write, even though the runtime terminal path has an approval service. That validation route cannot consume a receipt or present an approval request; the model can only see an unavailable gate.
findings.suggestedFix: Give hooks an explicit host execution policy and the run approval context. Preserve configured versus inferred trust, cancellation, and profile-preserving reruns instead of switching to user mode.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Exercise configured harmless one-liners under balanced/strict/allow-all, denial, unavailable context, and existing matching receipt; every result explains whether the hook ran and which authorization applied.

findings.title: Native smoke still requires exec to be an unimplemented stub

evidence.detail: Smoke invokes exec with EOF and expects exit 2/not_implemented.
Exec now delegates to the implemented runner.
EOF at the real handshake exits 1.
Linux matrix smoke flag is a YAML boolean.
CI references the stale script, but compares the boolean flag to string true.

findings.trigger: Run the native smoke against a fresh current openbuff-native binary.
findings.consequence: The built binary passes version and unknown-role probes, then the local script exits 1 with exec exited 1, expected 2 despite 19 passing Rust unit tests. The workflow references this incompatible check; its boolean/string condition mismatch makes actual CI execution potentially skipped, not established by this audit.
findings.suggestedFix: Test the real initialize/ExecPlan/payload/error contract, correct typed matrix guards, and retain explicit stub checks only for still-unimplemented roles; update the README role inventory.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Fresh locked/offline builds pass a smoke that executes a harmless target, handles EOF/malformed plans, and verifies honest enforced/degraded status. A host-runnable CI receipt confirms that the smoke/test steps actually ran rather than skipped.

findings.title: A reusable sidecar supervisor keeps the previous stop promise

evidence.detail: stopPromise is retained for the supervisor lifetime.
start permits stopped state.
stop only runs performStop when stopPromise is null.
New child resets stopRequested but never resets stopPromise.

findings.trigger: Call start, await stop, then start and stop again on the same supervisor.
findings.consequence: The second stop awaits the already-resolved prior promise and never stops the new child or changes its running state. This is a direct state-flow defect in an otherwise real helper; no default production constructor was found, so current product exposure is limited.
findings.suggestedFix: Make stop memoization belong to one process lifecycle, or explicitly prohibit restarting a stopped instance with a typed error.
findings.acceptanceProbe: With the existing fake-sidecar harness, repeat start/stop and assert each child exits and pending requests reject; race a stop during the second handshake.
findings.assuranceLimit: A local Bun/Python fake handshake timed out; that attempt is excluded from behavioral assurance. This finding rests on inspected control flow.

domainAssessment.security: Confirmed approval-classification/exact-identity defects and canonical credential inheritance (F1-F4). Intentional full-access and unrestricted network defaults are not treated as vulnerabilities. MCP explicit credential delegation and origin DNS policy are distinguished from implicit host inheritance.
domainAssessment.correctness: Leader settlement is not process-scope death (F5/F6); hooks lack the terminal approval seam (F8), native smoke contradicts implementation (F9), and supervisor stop memoization has a lifecycle defect (F10).
domainAssessment.state-mutation: Owner gates and one-shot receipt locking are strengths. Premature settlement removes kill authority; MCP eviction abandons transport resources. Durable broker/recovery integrity is outside this shard.
domainAssessment.error-handling: Terminal timeout/abort/spawn and hooks skipped/no-hooks have useful distinct states. Native malformed plans fail loudly and optional diagnostics fail open by design. Lifecycle errors often settle before the actual resource is gone; LSP/browser/generic adapters do not share terminal cleanup guarantees.
domainAssessment.performance: Inline output, UTF-8 capture, job rings/log quota, lazy LSP and sidecar frame/pending caps are concrete bounds. MCP eviction does not bound live resources, quota cleanup can leave work running, and successful SYNC spools lack an inspected total quota/expiry. LSP unconsumed stderr is a static backpressure hypothesis, not a measured throughput claim.
domainAssessment.dependency-hygiene: SDK/common declare MCP ^1.18.2; the inspected installation is 1.20.2, whose default stdio environment and 60-second request timeout matter to the trace. Rust pins toolchain 1.87.0, declares Linux-only Landlock, and builds locked/offline. No advisory/network vulnerability scan was performed and no CVE claim is made.
domainAssessment.test-coverage: Existing tests verify profile-preserving reruns, ownership, timeout output, abort windows, quota byte bounds, generic fake-sidecar failures and Chrome sandbox choices. They miss the concrete negative cases in F1-F10. Root-supplied 19 Rust tests plus fresh native probes establish a working standalone slice; stale smoke disproves current native CI compatibility.
domainAssessment.api-contract: Bundled runtime intentionally ignores template terminal profiles while a consumer comment still claims clamping. Exact-command approval hash claims are false for semantic whitespace. Hook approval context, process stopped/error meaning, generic versus native wire framing and reusable supervisor lifetime require explicit contracts. Default capability advertisement is honestly lexical/unrestricted/unwired.

coverageLimits: All 18 primary selections and 46 secondary selections were read; merged exact ranges are supplied. Large run.ts, run-agent-step.ts, terminal-command-policy.ts, browser-logs.ts and basher.ts were sampled at the recorded ranges, not audited line-for-line.

Native query_index/read_files tools are unavailable in this Codex session. Cached RETRIEVAL.json and picker searches were used only as navigation; current source was verified with line-numbered filesystem reads and bounded rg searches.

No source fixes, credentials/private configuration values, external requests, or real-user process effects. Python child sentinels and resistant processes lived under owned evidence fixtures; TMPDIR isolated background log creation and sweeps. Cleanup receipt confirms no known fixture child remains running.

Harmless integration probes were Linux-local, using pinned Bun 1.3.5 and direct Rust/Python. No Windows/macOS process-tree, real Chrome, language-server, live remote MCP, recovery PID-reuse behavior, or live GitHub workflow was exercised. Matrix booleans compared to string true are a static execution-guard concern; no actual GitHub step execution is claimed.

A Bun/Node26 child-output anomaly and a Bun/Python fake-sidecar handshake timeout were not diagnosed or treated as product findings. The failed supervisor probe contributes no successful behavioral assurance; F10 is static control-flow evidence.

MCP eviction probe replaced ESM connect before import and never started transports; live resource leakage is supported by source and dependency lifecycle, not by creating 65 real processes. Installed MCP 1.20.2 source is supplemental and excluded from the pinned structural receipt.

Mutation broker/receipts/recovery integrity belongs to pair06, language query/root/rename semantics to pair07, plugin/origin/descriptors to pair10, overall packaging to pair11, browser/3D interaction quality to pair13, and subagent supervision to pair03.

Historical SPEC D40/D48/D49 was read as plan context and excluded from structural files. Linux Landlock probe proves fixture access restriction only, not network, Unix-socket, syscall, installed-host or cross-platform isolation. No best-possible, latency, memory benchmark or CVE claims are made.
